note: Jehoahaz (Shallum) is Josiah's son.
Jehoiakim (Eliakim) is Josiah's son.
The people of the land make Jehoahaz king after Josiah dies at Megiddo.
Pharaoh Neco removes Jehoahaz and puts his brother Jehoiakim on the throne.
Brothers: both sons of Josiah by Hamutal, so full brothers.
Jehoiachin is Jehoiakim's son.
Jehoiachin reigns in his father's place.
Nebuchadnezzar replaces Jehoiachin with his uncle Mattaniah, renamed Zedekiah. Chronicles calls Zedekiah his "brother", meaning kinsman.
descendant (generations omitted): grandson through Shealtiel (Ezra 3:2) or Pedaiah (1 Chr 3:19).
descendant (generations omitted): Gedaliah is son of Ahikam son of Shaphan.
Amel-Marduk is Nebuchadnezzar's son (Babylonian sources); Scripture names him as the next king.
Evil-merodach becomes king of Babylon after Nebuchadnezzar (562 BC).
Shalmaneser V is Tiglath-pileser's son and successor (Assyrian sources; scholarly-consensus).
Sennacherib is Sargon II's son and successor (Assyrian sources; scholarly-consensus).
The prophet Jehu is the son of the seer Hanani.
Zechariah is the son of the high priest Jehoiada.
Xerxes I (Ahasuerus) is the son of Darius I (Persian sources; scholarly-consensus). Ezra lists their reigns in order.
Artaxerxes I is the son and successor of Xerxes I (Persian and Greek sources; scholarly-consensus).
Vashti is queen until she refuses the king's summons and is deposed.
The king makes Esther queen in his seventh year.
The high priest finds the book of the law and carries out Josiah's temple purge.
Josiah's secretary reads the newly found book of the law to the king.
Hilkiah hands the scroll to Shaphan.
Hilkiah and Shaphan consult the prophetess Huldah about the book.
Shaphan's sons Ahikam, Gemariah and Elasah protect and assist Jeremiah.
Hananiah breaks Jeremiah's yoke and promises a quick return; Jeremiah says God did not send him and predicts his death within the year.
Pashhur beats Jeremiah and puts him in the stocks; Jeremiah renames him "Terror on every side".
Ebed-melech rescues Jeremiah from the muddy cistern and receives a promise of safety.
He protests to the king that Jeremiah has been wronged and obtains permission to rescue him.
Jehoiakim burns Jeremiah's scroll and orders his arrest; Jeremiah condemns his injustice.
The king orders Baruch's arrest along with Jeremiah's, but the LORD hides them.
Jehoiakim has Uriah brought back from Egypt and executed.
Uriah prophesies "according to all the words of Jeremiah".
Jehoiakim becomes Nebuchadnezzar's vassal, then rebels.
Nebuchadnezzar besieges Jerusalem and deports Jehoiachin in 597 BC.
The new king of Babylon releases Jehoiachin from prison and gives him a place at his table.
Jeremiah declares that none of Coniah's offspring will prosper on David's throne.
Nebuzaradan is Nebuchadnezzar's captain of the guard and carries out his orders in Jerusalem.
He frees Jeremiah from his chains and lets him choose where to live.
He entrusts Jeremiah and the remnant of Judah to Gedaliah.
Nebuchadnezzar appoints Gedaliah governor over those left in Judah.
Jeremiah stays with Gedaliah at Mizpah.
Daniel reads the writing on the wall and announces the end of Belshazzar's kingdom.
Darius plans to set Daniel over the kingdom, is distressed by the lions' den decree, and rejoices at Daniel's rescue.
After Belshazzar is slain, Darius the Mede receives the kingdom (identification debated).
Cyrus entrusts the temple vessels to Sheshbazzar and makes him governor.
Zerubbabel leads after Sheshbazzar; some identify the two as one person (debated).
Darius confirms Cyrus's decree and funds the temple's completion under Zerubbabel.
Darius supplies sacrifices and asks the priests to pray for the king.
Nehemiah is the king's cupbearer; Artaxerxes grants him leave and letters to rebuild Jerusalem.
The king's letter commissions Ezra to teach and enforce God's law (date of Ezra's mission debated).
The king promotes Haman and gives him his signet ring.
The king honours Mordecai for saving his life and makes him second in the kingdom.
Enraged that Mordecai will not bow, Haman plots to destroy him and all the Jews.
Esther exposes Haman as the adversary and enemy of her people.
The governor of Samaria mocks, threatens and plots against Nehemiah's wall building.
Tobiah ridicules the work, sends letters to frighten Nehemiah, and is later thrown out of the temple storeroom.
The two act together against Nehemiah, even hiring a prophet to frighten him.
He sends envoys and a gift to Hezekiah, probably seeking an alliance against Assyria.
Isaiah warns that what Hezekiah showed the Babylonian envoys will one day be carried to Babylon.
As Pul he comes against Israel; Menahem pays a thousand talents of tribute.
He seizes Galilee and Gilead in Pekah's reign and deports their people.
Ahaz becomes his vassal to gain help against Aram and Israel; Chronicles says it brought distress, not strength.
Shalmaneser imprisons Hoshea for rebellion and besieges Samaria.
Isaiah's barefoot sign-act during Sargon's Ashdod campaign warns against trusting Egypt and Cush.
Comes to comfort Job but insists his suffering must be punishment; God rebukes him and has Job pray for him.
Comes to comfort Job, then argues his children died for their sin; rebuked by God.
Comes to comfort Job, then tells him God exacts less than his guilt deserves; rebuked by God.
Angry that Job justifies himself rather than God, he argues that suffering can be God's warning and instruction.
Elihu is angry with the three friends for condemning Job without answering him.

Shemaiah forbids war against the northern tribes and later calls Rehoboam to humble himself before Shishak's invasion.
Rehoboam's acts are recorded in the writings of Shemaiah the prophet and Iddo the seer.
Chronicles cites "the visions of Iddo the seer concerning Jeroboam".
Hanani rebukes Asa for relying on Aram; Asa puts him in the stocks.
His encouragement leads Asa to remove idols and renew the covenant.
Jehu announces the end of Baasha's dynasty.
He rebukes Jehoshaphat for helping Ahab, while noting the good found in him.
Oded confronts Pekah's returning army and persuades Israel to release its Judean captives.
Joash orders the stoning of Zechariah, the son of the priest who had raised him.
